Incipient

/in-SIP-ee-uhnt/ - the stress falls on SIP · adjective

Hear It

What It Means

Incipient means just beginning to exist or develop.

An incipient smile tugged at the witness's mouth before she caught it and looked down.

Worked Example

Walking the rows at dawn, the vineyard manager found incipient mildew on two leaves — a gray dust you'd miss from a meter away — and had the sprayer out before the dew burned off.

Incipient flags the very first stage of something that is developing — often something you'd rather stop. Where inchoate (this unit) describes the shapelessness of what has begun, incipient simply marks how early it is: the thing has just crossed the line into existing.

How Incipient Sits Among Its Neighbors

Synonyms — open each to see how it differs

budding

budding: beginning to grow — used of hopeful things: careers, friendships

emerging

emerging: coming into view, a stage past the very start

Antonyms

full-blown

full-blown: arrived at full force, nothing early about it

advanced

advanced: far along in its development

How Strong Is It? — incipient → developing → full-blown

developing vs. incipient

developing vs. incipient: Developing goes further than incipient: an incipient project has barely appeared, while a developing one is visibly under way.

full-blown vs. incipient

full-blown vs. incipient: Full-blown goes far beyond incipient — the storm has arrived in full force, with nothing 'just beginning' about it.

Sort It Out

Now place each word on the right side of incipient.

Build the Word

The pieces

Prefix — in-

Prefix — in-: in, on (not the negative in-)

Root — -cip-

Root — -cip-: to take (Latin capere)

Suffix — -ient

Suffix — -ient: adjective: doing

Put it together

Put it together: Another directional in-: in- ('in, on') + capere ('to take') gave incipere, 'to take in hand' — to begin. Incipient is the taking-in-hand stage, the first grip on existence. The same cip- sits in recipient, the one who takes delivery. Nothing here means 'not.'

Root Check

Word Choice

formal

Incipient is the clinician's and forecaster's word for a thing at its very first stage — incipient rust, incipient panic. It is neutral about shape (that is inchoate's job, one card back) and slightly wary in tone: what is incipient often wants catching early.
